Class MixIdea

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.MixIdea
public final class MixIdea extends Object
A plan the fighter is handed for its strafe keys, so that it fights with its feet as well: which side to go round the opponent on.

This is what players call AD strafing. One of A and D is held, and kept held: through the swing, through the recharge, while the weapon is ready, and through the next swings too, for MIN_CIRCLE_SWINGS to MAX_CIRCLE_SWINGS swings on end. The fighter goes round the opponent while its combo lands and has to keep turning to keep it in front; the opponent has to keep turning to hit back at all. Then comes another circle, to either side, or a straight run.

A straight run is MIN_STRAIGHT_SWINGS to MAX_STRAIGHT_SWINGS swings with no strafe at all: the W-tap combo, where the distance is kept with W alone (let go of after the hit, pressed again to come back to the edge of reach as the sword comes back). The user, 18 October: the strafe "dont need to be circle", "W tap combo as well cause like high tier player does it", though "circle combo does do really well". About a quarter of the swings; up to then one swing in seven between circles was made straight in, and nothing was asked of the keys on it.

(Up to 0.11.3 four plans in ten were something else: out to a side right after the swing and back the other way before the next. That is not how the keys are used in a fight.)

A plan can also say how long to hold the next swing back once the weapon is ready (allowHolds(boolean)). No stage uses that any more: a fighter that waits on a ready weapon gives hits away, and it proved not to be something that can be learned from a penalty.

Nothing here says anything about the opponent. The plan is an input (see ObsSpec.SC_IDEA_STRAFE) the network learns to follow; until it has, assist(int[], int, boolean) applies it to the chosen action directly.
